approval.note: Approved mTORC1 inhibitor (renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis >=13y; LAM adults). Carries a boxed warning.

claims.text: Rapamycin-class mTOR inhibition is senomorphic rather than senolytic: it selectively blunts the senescence-associated secretory phenotype by suppressing IL1A translation, reducing downstream NF-kB-driven cytokine secretion; in mice, rapamycin suppressed the ability of senescent fibroblasts to stimulate tumour growth.
A second mechanism study confirms mTOR controls the SASP at the translational level via MAPKAPK2, reinforcing that mTOR inhibitors dampen - rather than eliminate - the senescent program.

Disease-specific link: in monoallelic BubR1-mutant mice modelling MVA, predisposition to sarcopenia correlated with mTORC1 hyperactivity - the same tissue (skeletal muscle) that shows p16-driven senescence in BubR1 insufficiency. mTORC1 hyperactivity is a plausible, genotype-linked drug target.

Progeria precedent: rapamycin reversed the cellular phenotype of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria fibroblasts via autophagy activation - evidence that mTOR inhibition can modify progeroid cell biology, though HGPS is lamin-based, not checkpoint-based.

Genome-stability caveat: in yeast mutation-accumulation lines, rapamycin only marginally changed mutation rates but was associated with chromosome XII amplifications (a compensatory rDNA response); the long-term effect of chronic mTOR inhibition on karyotypic stability is not fully characterised.

BubR1 insufficiency engages p16Ink4a senescence in muscle and fat; suppressing the SASP (rather than killing the cells) may reduce tissue damage while preserving the senescence-mediated brake on aneuploid-cell expansion.

pediatric.boxed_warning: IMMUNOSUPPRESSION: 'Increased susceptibility to infection and the possible development of lymphoma and other malignancies may result from immunosuppression.' Also boxed: not recommended in liver/lung transplant (excess mortality, graft loss, bronchial anastomotic dehiscence). The malignancy warning is directly on-point for a cancer-predisposition syndrome.
pediatric.approved_pediatric_indication: Prophylaxis of organ rejection in renal transplant patients aged 13 years and older (quoted label fact). Safety and efficacy NOT established <13 years for transplant use, and <18 years for LAM.
pediatric.label_pediatric_dosing_fact: Adult/maintenance renal-transplant dosing is trough-guided; no established pediatric dosing below age 13 exists on this label (quoted label fact, not advice).
key_risks: Boxed-warning malignancy risk (lymphoma and other malignancies, particularly skin) in a child already predisposed to cancer (rhabdomyosarcoma in the HPO profile) - the single most important safety flag of any candidate.

Decline in renal function and proteinuria (label 5.8/5.9): nephrocalcinosis is in the child's HPO profile, so renal function is already a concern; label warns against chronic use with calcineurin inhibitors due to renal deterioration.

Hyperlipidaemia, impaired wound healing, interstitial lung disease/non-infectious pneumonitis, latent viral reactivation, live-vaccine contraindication, male infertility (future consideration), embryo-fetal toxicity.
Immunosuppression in a growing child: infection risk + reduced immune surveillance of emerging neoplastic clones - mechanistically counter to the cancer-interception goal.
monitoring: Sirolimus trough concentrations (label-recommended therapeutic drug monitoring)
Lipids, CBC, infection surveillance; no live vaccines

celegans.expected: lifespan extension plausible via conserved TOR-longevity link, but does not test aneuploidy directly

fibroblasts.assay: chronic low-dose sirolimus on MVA patient fibroblasts
fibroblasts.readout: SASP cytokines (IL6/IL8), p-S6 biomarker, aneuploidy rate (FISH/scDNA-seq), BubR1 level
fibroblasts.expected: SASP suppression without killing senescent cells; check it does not increase aneuploidy rate

scrnaseq.assay: SASP/inflammatory module reversal on patient signature

verdict_reason: Mechanistically the cleanest senomorphic: direct evidence that mTOR inhibition blunts the SASP (PMID:26147250, PMID:26280535) plus a genotype-specific hook - mTORC1 hyperactivity tracks sarcopenia in the BubR1-mutant MVA mouse model (PMID:31738183). But the boxed-warning immunosuppression/malignancy risk is squarely against the child's cancer-predisposition phenotype, and no pediatric approval exists below age 13. Shortlisted as a testable hypothesis with a hard safety gate: fibroblast and worm evidence of benefit must clear the immunosuppression concern before any clinical consideration.
